disclaimer: Scheme rules, amounts and deadlines change. Always confirm on the official portal, at your bank, Raitha Samparka Kendra, Common Service Centre (CSC) or Krishi Vigyan Kendra before applying.

schemes.name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
schemes.benefit: ₹6,000 per year paid in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 by Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the Aadhaar-seeded bank account of eligible landholding farmer families.
eligibility: Landholding farmer family (husband, wife and minor children) with cultivable land recorded in State/UT land records.
Land ownership records are verified; land acquired after 01-02-2019 is under special scrutiny.

Excluded: institutional landholders; families where a member is or was a constitutional post holder, minister, MP/MLA, mayor or district panchayat chairperson; serving or retired government employees (except Group D / multi-tasking staff); pensioners with monthly pension ≥ ₹10,000 (except Group D); income-tax payers in the last assessment year; registered doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects practising professionally.
how_to_apply: Register on pmkisan.gov.in (New Farmer Registration) or through a CSC / village agriculture officer.
Complete e-KYC (OTP, face authentication in the PM-KISAN app, or biometric at a CSC) — mandatory for receiving instalments.
Check beneficiary status on the portal using Aadhaar or registration number.

schemes.name: PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana) — crop insurance
schemes.benefit: Insurance cover for yield loss from natural calamities, pests and diseases, prevented sowing, localised risks and post-harvest losses. Farmer premium is capped at 2% of sum insured for Kharif food and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food and oilseed crops, and 5% for annual commercial/horticultural crops; the rest is paid by Central and State governments (50:50; 90:10 in North-Eastern and Himalayan states).
eligibility: All farmers, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers, growing notified crops in notified areas.
Voluntary for all farmers since Kharif 2020 (loanee farmers can opt out through their bank).
how_to_apply: Enrol through your bank, CSC, insurance company agent or the National Crop Insurance Portal (pmfby.gov.in) before the seasonal cut-off date notified for your district (typically July for Kharif and December for Rabi).
Report localised loss (e.g. hailstorm, inundation) to the insurer, bank or agriculture department within 72 hours, e.g. through the Crop Insurance app.

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / RBI / NABARD
schemes.benefit: Revolving short-term credit for crop cultivation, post-harvest expenses and allied activities (animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries). Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) crop loans are given at 7% per year, and farmers who repay promptly get a further 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive — an effective rate of 4%. The Union Budget 2025-26 announced raising the MISS loan limit from ₹3 lakh to ₹5 lakh; check with your bank how this applies to your account.
eligibility: Owner-cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, and self-help groups or joint liability groups of farmers.
Farmers engaged in animal husbandry and fisheries are also eligible.
how_to_apply: Apply at any commercial bank, regional rural bank or cooperative bank branch, or through the bank's online portal.
The credit limit is fixed from the scale of finance for your crops and your land area.

schemes.name: PMKSY – Per Drop More Crop (micro-irrigation)
schemes.benefit: Financial assistance for drip and sprinkler irrigation: 55% of the unit cost for small and marginal farmers and 45% for other farmers, for up to 5 hectares per beneficiary. Many states, including Karnataka, add a top-up subsidy.
eligibility: Farmers with their own land (or lease agreement where allowed) and a water source.
Small and marginal farmers receive the higher assistance rate.
documents: Quotation/design from a registered micro-irrigation company
how_to_apply: Apply through the State horticulture or agriculture department (in Karnataka, through the Raitha Samparka Kendra / horticulture office or the state online portal).
A registered supplier prepares the design and installs; subsidy is released after field verification.

schemes.name: Soil Health Card Scheme
schemes.benefit: Free soil testing of farm samples with a card reporting 12 parameters (N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC, organic carbon) and crop-wise fertiliser and amendment recommendations.
documents: Farmer details and survey number of the plot
how_to_apply: Soil samples are collected by the agriculture department in campaign mode; you can also contact the nearest soil testing laboratory or Raitha Samparka Kendra.
Download your card from the Soil Health Card portal.

schemes.name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
schemes.benefit: Online trading platform linking APMC mandis so farmers can sell to buyers beyond their local market with transparent price discovery and online payment.
eligibility: Farmers, FPOs and traders registered on the e-NAM portal or at an e-NAM-integrated APMC.
how_to_apply: Register at enam.gov.in or the e-NAM mobile app, or at the e-NAM help desk of an integrated mandi.

schemes.name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
schemes.benefit: Medium to long-term loans for post-harvest management and community farming assets (warehouses, cold storage, sorting/grading units, primary processing) with 3% per year interest subvention for up to 7 years on loans up to ₹2 crore, plus credit guarantee cover (CGTMSE / NABSanrakshan) for loans up to ₹2 crore. It is not a grant.
eligibility: Farmers, FPOs, PACS, self-help groups, joint liability groups, cooperatives, agri-entrepreneurs and start-ups.
how_to_apply: Apply on agriinfra.dac.gov.in and choose a participating lending institution.

schemes.name: PM-KMY (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana) — farmer pension
schemes.benefit: Minimum assured pension of ₹3,000 per month after age 60. The farmer contributes ₹55–₹200 per month depending on entry age and the Central Government contributes an equal amount. The spouse is entitled to 50% as family pension.
eligibility: Small and marginal farmers owning up to 2 hectares of cultivable land as per State/UT land records.
Excluded: those covered by other statutory social security schemes (NPS, ESIC, EPFO) and higher-income categories as per scheme guidelines.
how_to_apply: Enrol at a Common Service Centre (CSC) or on maandhan.in.
